key_insight: AlgoRAG shows that retrieval-augmented generation can deliver correct, pedagogically useful explanations for abstract theoretical computer science topics by grounding the LLM in curated course materials.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a practical blueprint for AI tutoring systems in math-intensive CS domains, where notation-aware retrieval and pedagogical ranking can improve answer quality beyond generic LLMs.
method: Built a domain-specific RAG knowledge base from textbooks, lecture slides, practice problems, worked proof templates, and worksheets.
Added mathematical entity recognition, notation-aware retrieval, and pedagogical re-ranking to improve proof and complexity-theory responses.
Evaluated on 179 exam-style questions across core TCS topics including asymptotic analysis, recurrences, dynamic programming, graph algorithms, NP-completeness, sorting, and divide-and-conquer.
evidence_signal: On 179 curated questions, AlgoRAG reported 100% success, 38.0 s mean response time, ROUGE-1 F1 of 0.0963, ROUGE-L F1 of 0.0683, and pedagogical quality of 0.7620; BLEU-4 was zero due to notation/paraphrase mismatch in proofs.
watch_item: The zero BLEU-4 score and relatively low lexical overlap indicate that standard text-similarity metrics may underrepresent correctness, so evaluation should include reasoning-aware human or task-specific assessment.
paper_title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory
